$comment: Holdout expectations, derived by hand from the doctrine's engine descriptions AFTER ruleDigest (sha256 of the concatenated rule surface named by RULE_SOURCES in packages/ds-codegen/src/analytical/necessity.ts) was recorded, and never tuned to the engine's output. Each expectation is a judgment in canonical tuple form: [code|term, subject, assertion, engine, evidenceClass]. If engines.ts changes, the digest check fails; the remedy is to re-derive every expectation by hand and re-record, not to copy the engine's output. Re-record log: 27701a78... (authored) -> 5fc0509d... after REL-UNIT-DIAGNOSTIC-CAUSE-RENAME-01 (identifier rename; no expectation changed) -> 493d9bd2... after REL-FIELD-ALGEBRA-02 Phase A (occurrence identity gained the assertion key and the emitting engine; the suppression obligation moved to declaration-missing; subjects lost the '#kind:op' suffix). Every item re-derived by hand in the new form; no code, subject locus, or evidence class changed. -> 6b7b2135... after REL-FIELD-ALGEBRA-02 Phase B (the kernel: capabilities replace scale labels, rollup is an aggregate, max is min's alias, target grain gone). Every item re-derived by hand against the kernel engine description; only two occurrence KEYS changed, both in FX_H_KPI_INDEX_AND_RATE (aggregate:max -> aggregate:min; rollup:sum(toGrain=quarter) -> aggregate:sum); no code, subject, engine, or evidence class changed. -> c2141c64... -> 9cb24f4e... -> 03db3460... -> 19853c84... across REL-VIEW-ALGEBRA-01. Four moves, one argument. The slice added the derivation boundary and wired it into judge() (c2141c64), then made the boundary three-valued and ran it BEFORE assertion evaluation so an unadmitted result cannot lend standing to assertions over it (9cb24f4e), then widened the digest's domain from engines.ts alone to the whole rule surface in RULE_SOURCES order, engines.ts then derivation.ts (03db3460) — because a digest over one module would let a rule move into the other and change freely while this file still claimed to be current — and finally replaced two literal NUL separator bytes in derivation.ts with spaces (19853c84), which git had been reading as a binary file and therefore refusing to diff. What discharges the re-derivation duty here is a REACH argument, not eight independent re-derivations: no fixture in fixtures.jsonl declares a derivedBy, so checkDerivations returns empty for every holdout item, the ungrounded set is empty, no assertion is withheld, and the boundary cannot reach any of these eight judgments. That argument was then checked mechanically — all eight items still match their recorded expectations exactly and all eight report zero derivation occurrences (tmp/reverify-holdout.mts). The expectations themselves were not touched, and no status, code, subject, assertion key, engine or evidence class changed. -> 732fd6bc... after the seven stage-2 rules the corpus demands were implemented (bin closure undeclared; normalize over a non-additive measure; a projection discarding nest membership; a subtotal off the declared hierarchy grain; peers at mixed temporal grains; peers aggregating one source to divergent target grains; flow conservation, as a diagnostic over rows and an obligation without them), the schema-evidence path for fan-out was added to the additivity engine, and the code vocabulary moved into codes.ts, which joins the rule surface. The reach argument still holds and is now checked more widely than the eight items: every new rule requires a derivedBy or a peers declaration, and no fixture in fixtures.jsonl has either, so analytical:check-baseline reports EVERY fixture's canonical judgment conserved byte-for-byte. The eight holdout items were also re-checked individually and all still match with zero derivation occurrences. -> 50ef443f... after the stage-2 fixtures landed and two more modules joined the rule surface: judgment.ts, whose deriveStatus decides what a set of occurrences MEANS, and structure.ts, whose normalizeObservation decides what a row says. Both move judgments as surely as a rule does, and neither was digested. The expectations below did not change and could not have: the reach argument is now MECHANICAL rather than written — stage1.test.ts asserts, per holdout item, that its derivation domain is empty, so the first holdout fixture that ever reaches the boundary fails loudly instead of being re-recorded quietly. -> b31eef8a... after `alphaRename` (structure.ts, on the rule surface) was repaired to carry `derivedBy` and `peers`. It had rebuilt each relation as `{grain, fields}` and each structure as `{relations}`, so the name-blind canonical form DROPPED every derivation and every peer set: two fixtures differing only in their derivation were the same representation, and a necessity witness naming a derivation coordinate would have passed NO_COLLISION without erasing anything. No judgment moved — the repair touches the quotient's view of a fixture, not the engine's — and both were checked: all eight items still match, and analytical:check-baseline reports every recorded judgment conserved. Note what this still does NOT cover: no HOLDOUT fixture exercises a derivation, so the boundary's own rules are held to the stage-2 case fixtures and unit tests rather than to a hand-authored answer key, and the first holdout item that declares a derivedBy will need its expectation derived by hand, not read off the engine. Re-recorded b31eef8a -> 96a93f54: derivation.ts gained the OPERATOR_LAWS locus, where project now refuses to reinterpret a field it retains (a retained name is not a retained field), and conservation now fails closed on unusable edge observations rather than skipping them — an unread edge is missing from both sides of the balance, so silence could turn an unbalanced graph into an apparently balanced one. REACH: both changes are inside checkDerivations, and every holdout item asserts an empty derivation domain, so neither can touch a holdout expectation. Re-verified by hand rather than re-run: no holdout fixture declares a derivedBy, so neither the project law nor the conservation walk has an input in any of them, and analytical:check-baseline reports every recorded judgment conserved. NON-CLAIM: this re-record does not re-derive the holdout expectations themselves, which remain the ones authored before the derivation domain existed; and because no holdout item reaches the boundary, these two repairs are held to the stage-2 fixtures and unit tests rather than to a hand-authored answer key. Re-recorded 96a93f54 -> 9d01b189: a COMMENT-ONLY edit in derivation.ts, correcting an overclaim that co-locating a law statement with its certifier makes the two incapable of drifting. It does not; it removes the possibility of a competing law authority and puts the prose where an editor of the check will see it, while the falsifiers are what make each law operational. REACH: no rule changed, so no judgment can have moved — the digest covers the rule surface byte-for-byte, which is why a comment moves it at all. Verified by re-running the full analytical suite and analytical:check-baseline, both unchanged. NON-CLAIM: a digest that moves on a comment cannot distinguish a documentation edit from a rule edit, so the discharge here is the diff, not the digest. REACH DISCHARGED (no digest move — ruleDigest stays 9d01b189 because no RULE_SOURCES file changed; what moved is what the holdout can SEE): three items were added that reach the derivation boundary, closing the gap this log recorded as an explicit non-claim twice. FX_H_ORDERS_FLATTENED_REINTERPRETS_AMOUNT holds the project law — a projection that retains `amount` by name while redeclaring it ratio -> interval is a reinterpretation wearing the old name, so the result is not derivable (illegal). FX_H_ROUTES_CONSERVED_ONE_EDGE_UNREADABLE holds the fail-closed conservation walk — one edge observation is unreadable, an unread edge is missing from both sides of the balance, and the check cannot decide either way (unproven). It was chosen to separate `cannot be decided` from `conserved`: under the older skip-the-row behaviour it would report NOTHING, because dropping the unreadable edge leaves the middle node balanced 10 in / 10 out and the last node a pure sink the walk skips. FX_H_ORDERS_FLATTENED_DROPS_REGION is the CONTROL, differing from the first item in exactly one fact — whether the retained field's declaration is preserved — and it is admissible: what a projection drops is derived, not declared, so the dropped field's declaration is irrelevant. All three expectations were hand-derived from the stated operator laws and written BEFORE the engine was run on any of them; the engine then matched all three exactly, including status, occurrence kind, code or term, subject, derivation key, engine and evidence class. The eight original items keep their pre-boundary expectations and are still held to an EMPTY derivation domain — stage1.test.ts now asserts empty only for items that do not record the domain, so an item with a hand-derived derivation expectation is held to that expectation instead of failing for having one. NON-CLAIM: three items exercise two of the seven operator laws (project, graph-conservation) and none of the other five; aggregate-to-grain, join, nest, bin and normalize are still held to the stage-2 case fixtures and unit tests rather than to a hand-authored answer key.
